A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VGCURE benchmark and MCDGraph framework. Their text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 14 LVLMs, MCDGraph fine-tuning experiments, and graph-structure and complexity analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds backbone-LLM comparisons, error analysis, downstream evaluations, and visual-style and naming robustness experiments.

M1.justification: The three MCDGraph tasks, their inputs and outputs, Equations 1–3, and LoRA fine-tuning procedure are retained. The added explanation for supplying text triples during masked infilling clarifies an existing input rather than introducing a component.

E1.justification: The original 22-task benchmark remains, but v2 adds VisionGraph connectivity, cycle and maximum-flow evaluations, FACTKG fact verification, and ScienceQA and AOKVQA. It also evaluates text-triple inputs, two alternative visual styles, and Node-Edge and Name-R naming conditions, substantially extending task and input coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 4 adds Qwen2 and InternLM2 as text-only backbone comparators against Qwen2-VL and InternVL2. The original 14-model benchmark comparison and the base-versus-MCDGraph comparator pairs remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include sampling 1,000 examples per task for text-triple backbone testing, excluding CP from that comparison, and using 50 graphs per structure for generalization testing. Downstream and ordinary VQA evaluations are also introduced. These supplement the retained benchmark protocol and training regimen; the PDFs do not indicate revisions to the original experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds a perception-versus-backbone diagnostic comparison, six categories of errors with examples, visual-style and naming robustness tests, and assessment of ordinary VQA performance after fine-tuning. The original complexity analyses and Nested Relation Query case are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars. Averaging over graph structures and the existing metric aggregation practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Original Tables 3–5 and the detailed appendix QA/FC scores are unchanged. v2 adds backbone/error findings and Tables 6 and 11–15; newly reported Qwen2-VL versus MCDGraph results include maximum-flow scores of 1.72/5.17 and ScienceQA accuracies of 85.13/81.31. Section 3.2 also corrects the EN ceiling from 16.28% to 16.38%, matching the unchanged Table 3.

T1.justification: The task formulations, graph-generation specifications and three method equations retain their mathematical content. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and v2 introduces no new formal derivation or assumption.

C1.justification: The benchmark, fundamental-capability diagnosis and three-task framework remain the core contributions. v2 broadens the abstract's explicit effectiveness claim to downstream graph tasks and adds unseen-style generalization in the introduction. v1 already positioned the method for downstream use but emphasized demonstrated benefits on fundamental tasks and structural complexity.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving weak visual perception, backbone reasoning limitations and six failure categories. It interprets naming sensitivity, acknowledges unaddressed semantic reasoning in FACTKG and ordinary VQA degradation, and explains the retained case study. The limitations concerning a single visual style and absent real-world validation are removed, while graph-size and larger-model limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendices C.1 and E add text-triple evaluation prompts, NetworkX/Matplotlib rendering information and alternative naming instructions. The training sample mixture, LoRA hyperparameters, hardware and code/data access disclosures are retained from v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for FACTKG, ScienceQA, AOKVQA and several introductory and metric-related works, while removing MolCA and v1's NLGraph-associated citation. The central positioning against task-specific graph reasoning approaches remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The seven-section main narrative and most method/setup prose remain. v2 condenses the introduction, task descriptions, related work and conclusion, adds diagnostic/downstream subsections, reorganizes appendix labels, and adds Jun Yu to the author list.

P2.justification: New backbone radar plots, error diagrams, style examples and downstream/generalization tables substantially expand the displays. Main Figures 2 and 3 are condensed; the original full QA radar figure moves to v2 Figure 12, and existing tables and complexity plots are redistributed across the main text and appendices.

improvement.justification: v2 makes applicability and failure modes more assessable through downstream tests, style/naming experiments, perception/error analysis and disclosure of VQA losses, addressing gaps explicitly acknowledged in v1. The net gain is limited by sparse downstream protocol details, mixed or small gains in Table 6, and Appendix E's overly broad assertion that style has no effect. The added evidence improves coverage and transparency, but only partly supports the broader generalization claims.
